headline: The Dow closed above 50,000 for the first time on Nov 24 (+0.85%) while the Nasdaq fell 1.48% and chips gave back Monday's rally; Oct PCE and Q3 GDP are due at 8:30am ET with a December Fed hike about 95-96% priced.
regime: Hiking regime with a volatile, rotating tape: the Fed funds target is 3.75-4.00%, a 25bp hike on Dec 9 is about 95-96% priced (CME FedWatch), the 10-year is 4.90%, and the VIX eased to 26.4 from 35.9 on Friday.

lean.why: Futures were slightly lower late Tuesday (S&P -0.2%) ahead of PCE and GDP at 8:30am ET; US markets are closed Thursday.
A Dec 9 hike is about 95-96% priced; the jobs report (Dec 4), FOMC (Dec 9) and CPI (Dec 10) follow, and the S&P is 7.9% below its Oct 6 peak.
A hiking Fed with a 4.90% 10-year yield pressures multiples, while strong earnings (Dell, retail) and a Dow at 50,000 show breadth.

news.head: PCE and GDP due before Thanksgiving, with a December hike nearly priced
news.srcN: CNBC via Gotrade, Nov 24-25; Stocktwits, Nov 24
news.mean: Oct PCE is due at 8:30am ET Wednesday. Consensus is headline +0.3% m/m and 3.8% y/y, with core +0.3% m/m (Bloomberg survey via Stocktwits); XTB lists Q3 GDP at 3.5% annualized and claims near 200K, though its core y/y figure is internally inconsistent. Futures were slightly lower late Tuesday (Dow -0.1%, S&P -0.2%).
news.hist: Rule of thumb: a hotter-than-expected core PCE usually pushes yields up and growth stocks down, and the reverse for a cooler print; there is no fixed size.
news.today: The release lands at 8:30am ET, so the first move at the open may be driven by core PCE versus about +0.3% m/m.
news.later: Investors may watch whether inflation stays near 3-4% when the Fed is already leaning toward a hike.

news.head: December Fed hike about 95-96% priced; Williams backs it
news.mean: CME FedWatch shows about 95-96% for a 25bp hike at the Dec 8-9 meeting and the rest on 50bp; Polymarket and Kalshi show 94% for a hike. Capp Notes says NY Fed President Williams backed a December hike and Gov. Waller has favored a possible 50bp move. The funds target is 3.75-4.00%.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: markets that already price a move at 95% tend to react more to the guidance than to the move itself.
news.today: Fed-speaker headlines and today's PCE may shift 50bp odds more than the 25bp odds.
news.later: Investors may weigh how many further hikes the Fed signals at the Dec 9 meeting.

news.head: Dow closes above 50,000 for the first time as Nasdaq slides 1.48%
news.srcN: Capp Notes, Nov 24; The Company Chronicle, Nov 24
news.mean: The Dow rose 0.85% to 50,018.70, the S&P 500 fell 0.50% to 7,201.09 (its 8th loss in 9 sessions, 7.9% below the Oct 6 peak), the Nasdaq fell 1.48% to 23,733.54 and the Russell 2000 gained 0.57%. Health care rose 2.95% while tech fell 3.26%. VIX closed at 26.36 versus 35.89 on Friday.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: rotation days, where defensive sectors rise while tech falls, often show up when leadership is being questioned.
news.today: Watch whether the rotation out of tech continues or reverses after PCE.
news.later: Investors may consider how concentrated their holdings are in the chip names that are swinging 5-10% a day.

news.head: AI chips give back Monday's rally: Micron -11%, AMD -8.9%, Nvidia -5.9%
news.srcN: Stock Titan, Nov 24; Capp Notes, Nov 24
news.mean: After Monday's surge, Nvidia fell 5.86% to $155.38, Micron 11.01% to $629.79, AMD 8.86% to $413.27, Broadcom 3.98% to $301.08 and Intel 8.15%. SOXX fell 8.27% on the day (Capp Notes).
news.hist: Rule of thumb: after a very large one-day jump, partial give-backs the next day are common, but there is no fixed pattern.
news.today: Chip names are moving 5-10% a day, so position size matters more than direction.
news.later: Investors may watch whether the memory and AI-capex story holds after the results from Dell and HPE.

news.head: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO; stock jumped 31% Monday
news.mean: Nvidia's board reinstated Huang as President and CEO (an 8-K press release says the vote was unanimous and cites input from senior US officials). The stock rose 31.48% Monday, then fell 5.86% to $155.38 Tuesday. A House interview with Huang is reported for Dec 1.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: leadership changes tied to government scrutiny tend to keep a stock headline-driven until the process ends.
news.today: Headlines on the Dec 1 House interview and export controls may move the name.
news.later: Long-term holders may watch the new export-control committee and the compliance hire.

news.head: Dell beats on AI servers: $54.9B revenue, $132.3B AI backlog
news.srcN: CNBC via Gotrade, Nov 24-25; Stock Titan, Nov 24
news.mean: Dell reported revenue of $54.94B vs $49.32B expected and adjusted EPS of $9.45 vs $6.59, with AI server sales of $22B (+291%) and a backlog of $132.3B. It guided Q4 EPS to $8.40 and revenue to about $56.3B. The stock closed at $295.28 (-11.83%) before results and was roughly flat to up about 1% after hours.
react: Sold off on margins the same day
news.hist: Rule of thumb: a big beat that barely moves the stock can mean the good news was already priced in.
news.today: Watch whether the after-hours calm holds at the open.
news.later: Investors may compare Dell's AI backlog with HPE's margin warning.

news.head: HPE, Analog Devices, Semtech and Ambarella plunge on guidance
news.mean: HPE fell 16.31% to $40.19 despite 50% revenue growth because adjusted gross margin fell 2.2 points; Analog Devices fell 17.37%, Semtech 16.97% and Dycom 18.02%. Ambarella fell 37.55% after hours on a Q4 revenue forecast of $70-75M versus $115.2M in Q3, with the CEO citing rising memory prices.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: when strong sales growth meets falling margins or guidance, stocks often drop even on beats.
news.today: Memory-price costs are the common thread to watch in other hardware names.
news.later: Investors may watch whether rising memory prices squeeze margins across hardware.

news.head: Retail earnings pop: Kohl's, Abercrombie, Dick's and Dollar Tree jump
news.mean: Kohl's rose 19.48% (Q3 sales +1.3% to $3.5B, outlook raised), Abercrombie 19.69% (record $1.4B sales, EPS outlook $13.70-13.90), Dick's 14.59% and Dollar Tree 11.18% (revenue +6.9% to $5.1B); Best Buy rose 2.70% on comparable sales +6.1%.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: retailers that raise outlooks heading into the holidays often rally, but large one-day pops can fade.
news.today: The holiday-season read is the theme for the next few days.
news.later: Investors may weigh whether strong results reflect spending or price increases.

news.head: Sanofi to buy Insmed for $41B in cash; Insmed +14%
news.mean: Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for $175 per share in cash, about $41.0B, closing expected in the first half of 2027 pending shareholder and regulatory approval. Insmed rose 14.13% to $170.15 and Sanofi 10.97%.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: takeover targets usually trade at a small discount to the offer until the deal closes, reflecting approval risk and time.
news.today: Biotech M&A headlines can lift the group briefly.
news.later: Investors may watch for more large-cap pharma deals as patents expire.

news.head: Consumer confidence jumps to 103.3, highest since early 2025
news.mean: The Conference Board index rose 11.4 points to 103.3 versus a 92.2 forecast; the Present Situation index was 132.8 and Expectations 83.6, while 12-month inflation expectations were 5.7%.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: strong confidence readings can support spending but also support a Fed that is leaning toward tightening.
news.today: Retail names were strong on the data and on earnings.
news.later: Investors may weigh high inflation expectations (5.7%) against stronger sentiment.

news.head: Gold falls 2.6% to about $3,555, near a 14-month low; silver -5.6%
news.srcN: Capp Notes, Nov 24; Stock Titan/Vista, Nov 24
news.mean: Gold settled near $3,553-3,555 (-2.6% to -2.7%) and silver fell 5.65% to $40.71, while the dollar index was 103.83 (-0.47%). Sources differ slightly on the settle (about $3,552-3,555).
news.hist: Rule of thumb: gold often weakens when real yields rise and the Fed is expected to hike.
news.today: Watch whether PCE moves yields and gold together.
news.later: Investors may weigh gold's fall against its larger gain over the longer period.

news.head: WTI rises 2% to about $82 as Iran sanctions and strike talk continue
news.mean: WTI closed near $82.05 (+2.35%, Capp Notes; $81.53, +1.7% per The Company Chronicle). New US sanctions hit Iran's shadow banking network (about $15B of activity), Qatar is working to revive US-Iran talks, and a US official said Washington is ready for strikes if needed. Stocktwits reports retail gasoline at $3.81, down 15% since September.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: oil spikes tied to geopolitical headlines often reverse if supply is not actually disrupted.
news.today: Iran and Qatar headlines may move crude intraday.
news.later: Investors may watch whether gasoline prices keep falling, which would ease inflation.

news.head: Anthropic closes below its $83 IPO price at $81.90
news.mean: Anthropic (ANT) fell 6.54% to $81.90 on Nov 24, below its $83 IPO price, as the AI trade sold off.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: recent IPOs that trade below their offer price often stay volatile until a first earnings report.
news.today: Watch whether the offer price acts as a floor or ceiling.
news.later: Investors may wait for more filings and results before drawing conclusions.

playbook: Homebuilders, REITs, utilities, small caps and unprofitable growth are pressured first. Banks and the dollar hold up better.
Housing, small caps, growth and gold benefit. Mortgage rates ease a few weeks later.
Gold and miners, emerging markets and big multinationals gain. Importers lose.
Airlines, cruise lines and shippers win. Energy stocks lose. Headline inflation eases.
A growth and small-cap rally is the usual response. Banks lose some margin tailwind.
Bonds rally, defensives (healthcare, staples, utilities) lead. Cyclicals and banks get hit by recession worries.
